title: A measured value is calibrated by its local unit rather than being a portable ordinal
summary: Distinguish unit-calibrated quantity interpretation from a fixed ordinal interpretation when the same value slot appears with different local unit frames.

design.mechanism: The written value is interpreted through a local unit or measure frame, so equal surface values can denote different quantities across calibrated units; an ordinal model assigns one portable rank.
design.unit: Complete value spans with independently bound unit/measure frame, value surface and cross-context calibration relation.
design.contrast: Unit-calibrated measurement versus invariant ordinal value, with value surface and position matched.
design.prediction: A calibrated model predicts context-dependent quantity ratios or ordered conversions when unit changes; an ordinal model predicts invariant rank and no unit-dependent conversion.
design.falsifier: Held cases with independently bound differing units show invariant rank and no calibration effect, or no unit contrast can be bound without importing the proposed meaning.
design.scope: Existing value/amount frames only; no raw TSV or new measurements; independent unit endpoint availability_unknown.
design.related: Near IDEA000014/21 and GDT627/GDT686 quantity/value routes, but asks calibration invariance across unit frames rather than conservation, attachment, or unit-word recurrence.
design.countermodel: A renderer can assign local amount prose to a fixed ordinal without the underlying value being calibrated.

source_evidence.quote:
GDT626 found a bounded four-cell ending but could only call it “value I–IV.”
GDT627 supplies the missing head semantics. The same written slot is reused
productively:

```text
quality head + a + value  = quality in degree I/II/III/IV
d            + a + value  = free measure or grade I/II/III/IV
```

In a plant-part list, the practical default for the second construction is a
local amount or dose. Thus `daiin` no longer means a generic operation and no
longer remains the opaque “d-value III.” It reads **three local measures or
portions**, with the kind of unit still open.

design.intake_limit: Raw proposal retained for later method review. Missing independently bound endpoints or identical model predictions are design/capacity stops, not empirical refutations. Source working glosses do not supply semantic gold.
